memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"He shall burn all the fat on the altar as he burned the fat of the fellowship offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man's sin, and he will be forgiven."'" - Lev 4:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the second time in this chapter, the same conclusion: he will be forgiven.

God keeps saying it. Verse 20 for the community. Verse 26 for the leader. It will come twice more before the chapter ends. Four times God stamps the same verdict on four different categories of sinner.

Why the repetition? Because guilt is stubborn. The human heart does not accept forgiveness after hearing it once. We need it said again, and again, and again.

If you have ever wondered why the same gospel truth has to be preached to you every Sunday when you already know it — this is why. Knowing something and believing it in the place where guilt lives are two different things.

Notice too the comparison: as he burned the fat of the fellowship offering. God links the sin offering back to the offering of celebration. The forgiven leader is not merely let off. He is restored to fellowship. The relationship resumes.

That is what forgiveness accomplishes. Not just the removal of a penalty, but the restoration of a friendship. The father in Jesus' parable did not simply pardon his son; he put a robe on him and threw a feast (Lk 15:22-24).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which truth about God's forgiveness do I need to hear again today?
2. Do I believe forgiveness restores relationship, or only cancels punishment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, say it to me again — that I am forgiven in Christ. And bring me back not just to safety but to closeness with You. Amen.
